#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""HQ vinyls: HQVINYLS/CARS/<car>.hqv in the game folder, the vinyls of
AdrienShadow's "High Quality Vinyls & Doorlines (1024x Upscaled)"
(nfsmods.xyz/mod/8064) for the browser's runtime, which paints a car's skin a
second time at 1024x1024 from them when a player has the mod on (Mods tab).

    .venv/bin/python tools/hqvinyls.py <game folder> --mod <the mod's zip or folder> [--quality 50] [--jobs N]

<the mod's zip> is "High Quality Vinyls & Doorlines v1.0.zip" as it comes (5.8 GB), or the folder it unpacks to.
It needs numpy and Pillow with AVIF (Pillow 11.3 or newer), and a C compiler for speed (cc; without one the
textures unpack in Python, hours instead of minutes).

The mod's installer replaces every car's CARS/<car>/VINYLS.BIN with one whose 1,788 textures are 1024x1024
A8R8G8B8, and the paint target DUMMY_SKIN1-6 with 1024 ones, which the game's compositor (0x611F10, one pixel of
the target per pixel of each layer) then fills at 1024.  The port keeps the game's own files: the game paints its
512 skin as always, and the runtime paints the same layers again at 1024 on the GPU from this pack.

A pack holds, per texture of the car's VINYLS.BIN and per doorline of its TEXTURES.BIN (<car>_DOORLINE, _KIT,
_WIDEBODY and their _MASK: the mod's Installation/ModData/CARTEMPLATETEXTURES_), the mod's picture as AVIF:
  - cleaned: the upscaler left faint noise (values 1-4) over 13-21% of the empty black; every pixel more than two
    of the game's texels away from anything in the game's own 512 picture is set to 0 (it blended at most 3% before)
  - masks (<vinyl>_MASK: the compositor reads their G) and grey pictures (the game's has R = G = B) as one channel,
    the G; colour pictures (R, G, B pick the vinyl's three colours) as three, 4:4:4
  - each vinyl followed by its mask (894 pairs a car), each doorline by its mask
  - no alpha: the mod's are all 255 (it took the game's off before upscaling).  The game's alpha is the skin's gloss
    where a picture is drawn as it is (a doorline, a vinyl without REMAP): the runtime sends the game's own 512 one
  - quality 50: mean error 1.6 (grey) and 2.4 (colour) of 255, ~5 and ~8 KB a picture (350Z, measured)

File layout (little-endian; tools/packcheck.py checks it, runtime/hqvinyls.c and the page read it):
  0   'HQV1'
  4   u32 version (1)
  8   u32 count
  12  u32 data start (= 16 + 16 * count, rounded up to 16)
  16  count x { u32 name hash, u32 offset (from the file's start), u32 size, u16 side, u8 channels (1, 3), u8 0 }
      sorted by hash
  ..  the AVIF pictures, each where its row says
"""
import argparse, ctypes, io, os, struct, subprocess, sys, tempfile, zipfile
from multiprocessing import Pool

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
from texpacks import chunks, tpks, textures, jdlz as jdlz_py, huff, bstring_hash, find  # noqa: E402

MAGIC, VERSION, ROW = b'HQV1', 1, 16
SIDE = 1024
ARGB, P8 = 21, 41
UNPACKED_HQ = SIDE * SIDE * 4 + 0x9C                # the mod's: level 0 only, then TextureInfo + platform info
UNPACKED_GAME = 350748                              # the game's: P8 512x512, 7 levels, palette, TextureInfo, platform
GAME_PAL = 0x55580
GROW = 2                                            # the game's texels around its picture that keep the mod's pixels
DOORLINES = ('_DOORLINE', '_DOORLINE_MASK', '_DOORLINE_KIT', '_DOORLINE_KIT_MASK', '_DOORLINE_WIDEBODY',
             '_DOORLINE_WIDEBODY_MASK')

# ---- JDLZ in C (the mod's 4 MB pictures: ~0.5 ms each against ~1.5 s in Python) ----------------------------------
JDLZ_C = r'''
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
long jdlz(const uint8_t *b, long csize_in, uint8_t *out, long cap){
    if (csize_in < 0x12 || memcmp(b, "JDLZ", 4)) return -1;
    uint32_t size, csize; memcpy(&size, b + 8, 4); memcpy(&csize, b + 12, 4);
    if ((long)csize != csize_in || (long)size > cap) return -1;
    long s = 0x12, o = 0, left = (long)csize - 0x12;
    unsigned f1 = b[0x10] | 0x100, f2 = b[0x11] | 0x100;
    while (left){
        if (f1 & 1){
            if (s + 2 > (long)csize) return -1;
            long ln, dist;
            if (f2 & 1){ ln = (((b[s] & 0xF0) << 4) | b[s+1]) + 3; dist = (b[s] & 0x0F) + 1; }
            else { dist = (((b[s] & 0xE0) << 3) | b[s+1]) + 17; ln = (b[s] & 0x1F) + 3; }
            if (o < dist || ln > (long)size - o || left < 2) return -1;
            for (long k = 0; k < ln; k++) out[o + k] = out[o + k - dist];
            o += ln; s += 2; left -= 2; f2 >>= 1;
        } else {
            if (o < (long)size){ if (s >= (long)csize) return -1; out[o++] = b[s++]; }
            left -= 1;
        }
        f1 >>= 1;
        if (f1 == 1){ if (!left || s >= (long)csize) return -1; f1 = b[s++] | 0x100; left--; }
        if (f2 == 1){ if (!left || s >= (long)csize) return -1; f2 = b[s++] | 0x100; left--; }
    }
    return o == (long)size ? o : -1;
}
'''
_lib = None


def jdlz_fast_init():
    global _lib
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='hqvinyls-')
    src, lib = os.path.join(d, 'jdlz.c'), os.path.join(d, 'jdlz.so')
    with open(src, 'w') as f: f.write(JDLZ_C)
    try:
        subprocess.run(['cc', '-O2', '-shared', '-fPIC', '-o', lib, src], check=True, capture_output=True)
        _lib = ctypes.CDLL(lib)
        _lib.jdlz.restype = ctypes.c_long
        _lib.jdlz.argtypes = [ctypes.c_char_p, ctypes.c_long, ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_long]
    except (OSError, subprocess.CalledProcessError):
        print('no C compiler: unpacking in Python (slow)', file=sys.stderr)
        _lib = False


def unpack(blob, cap):
    """a texture's block (JDLZ or HUFF), unpacked; None if it is neither or does not unpack within cap bytes"""
    try:
        if blob[:4] == b'JDLZ':
            size = struct.unpack_from('<I', blob, 8)[0]
            if size > cap: return None
            if _lib:
                out = ctypes.create_string_buffer(size)
                return out.raw if _lib.jdlz(blob, len(blob), out, size) == size else None
            return jdlz_py(blob)
        if blob[:4] == b'HUFF':
            return huff(blob, max_output_bytes=cap)
    except (ValueError, SystemExit, IndexError):
        return None
    return None


def packed_rows(d):
    """{name hash: its packed block} of a compressed texture pack (VINYLS.BIN)"""
    rows = {}
    for b, e in tpks(d, 0, len(d)):
        for cid, cb, ce in chunks(d, b, e):
            if cid != 0xB3310000: continue
            part = {c: (x, y) for c, x, y in chunks(d, cb, ce)}
            if 0x33310003 not in part: continue
            tb, te = part[0x33310003]
            for i in range((te - tb) // 24):
                nh, off, size = struct.unpack_from('<3I', d, tb + i * 24)
                if off + size <= len(d): rows[nh] = (off, size)
    return rows


# ---- one car ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def game_picture(blob):
    """the game's 512 picture of a vinyl texture: (RGB array 512x512x3, grey?) or None"""
    import numpy as np
    u = unpack(blob, UNPACKED_GAME)
    if not u or len(u) != UNPACKED_GAME or struct.unpack_from('<I', u, len(u) - 0x20 + 0x14)[0] != P8: return None
    w, h = struct.unpack_from('<HH', u, len(u) - 0x9C + 0x44)
    if (w, h) != (512, 512): return None
    ix = np.frombuffer(u, np.uint8, 512 * 512).reshape(512, 512)
    pal = np.frombuffer(u, np.uint8, 1024, GAME_PAL).reshape(256, 4)
    rgb = pal[ix][..., [2, 1, 0]]
    return rgb, bool((rgb[..., 0] == rgb[..., 1]).all() and (rgb[..., 1] == rgb[..., 2]).all())


def mod_picture(blob):
    """the mod's 1024 picture: BGRA array or None"""
    import numpy as np
    u = unpack(blob, UNPACKED_HQ)
    if not u or len(u) != UNPACKED_HQ: return None
    w, h = struct.unpack_from('<HH', u, len(u) - 0x9C + 0x44)
    if (w, h) != (SIDE, SIDE) or struct.unpack_from('<I', u, len(u) - 0x20 + 0x14)[0] != ARGB: return None
    return np.frombuffer(u, np.uint8, SIDE * SIDE * 4).reshape(SIDE, SIDE, 4)


def keep_area(rgb512):
    """where the mod's pixels are kept: the game's picture's pixels, grown by GROW texels, at 1024"""
    import numpy as np
    from PIL import Image, ImageFilter
    g = Image.fromarray(rgb512.any(-1).astype(np.uint8) * 255).filter(ImageFilter.MaxFilter(2 * GROW + 1))
    return np.asarray(g.resize((SIDE, SIDE), Image.Resampling.NEAREST)) > 0


def avif(bgra, keep, grey, quality):
    """the cleaned picture as AVIF bytes, and its channel count"""
    import numpy as np
    from PIL import Image
    if grey:
        a = np.where(keep, bgra[..., 1], 0).astype(np.uint8)
        im, kw, ch = Image.fromarray(a), {}, 1
    else:
        a = np.where(keep[..., None], bgra[..., [2, 1, 0]], 0).astype(np.uint8)
        im, kw, ch = Image.fromarray(np.ascontiguousarray(a)), {'subsampling': '4:4:4'}, 3
    b = io.BytesIO()
    im.save(b, 'AVIF', quality=quality, speed=6, **kw)
    return b.getvalue(), ch


class Mod:
    """the mod's files, from its zip or its unpacked folder"""
    def __init__(self, src):
        self.src, self.zip, self.root = src, None, None
        if os.path.isdir(src):
            self.root = src
        else:
            self.zip = zipfile.ZipFile(src)
            self.names = {n.replace('\\', '/').split('v1.0/', 1)[-1].upper(): n for n in self.zip.namelist()}

    def read(self, rel):
        rel = rel.replace('\\', '/')
        if self.zip:
            n = self.names.get(rel.upper())
            return self.zip.read(n) if n else None
        for top in (self.root, os.path.join(self.root, 'High Quality Vinyls & Doorlines v1.0')):
            p = find(top, rel)
            if p:
                with open(p, 'rb') as f: return f.read()
        return None

    def cars(self):
        if self.zip:
            return sorted({k.split('/')[1] for k in self.names if k.startswith('CARS/') and k.endswith('/VINYLS.BIN')})
        top = self.root if find(self.root, 'CARS') else os.path.join(self.root, 'High Quality Vinyls & Doorlines v1.0')
        cars = find(top, 'CARS')
        return sorted(c.upper() for c in os.listdir(cars) if find(os.path.join(cars, c), 'VINYLS.BIN')) if cars else []


def dds_argb(b):
    """a 1024x1024 A8R8G8B8 DDS (the mod's doorlines): BGRA array or None"""
    import numpy as np
    if not b or len(b) < 128 + SIDE * SIDE * 4 or b[:4] != b'DDS ': return None
    h, w = struct.unpack_from('<II', b, 12)
    flags, four, bits = struct.unpack_from('<III', b, 80)
    if (w, h) != (SIDE, SIDE) or four or bits != 32: return None
    return np.frombuffer(b, np.uint8, SIDE * SIDE * 4, 128).reshape(SIDE, SIDE, 4)


def one_car(job):
    game, mod_src, car, quality, out_dir = job
    if _lib is None: jdlz_fast_init()
    mod = Mod(mod_src)
    gp = find(game, f'CARS/{car}/VINYLS.BIN')
    mb = mod.read(f'CARS/{car}/VINYLS.BIN')
    if not gp or not mb: return car, 0, 0, [f'{car}: no VINYLS.BIN in the game or the mod']
    with open(gp, 'rb') as f: gd = f.read()
    grows, mrows = packed_rows(gd), packed_rows(mb)
    ents, notes = [], []
    both = set(grows) & set(mrows)
    masks = {hash_append(nh, '_MASK') for nh in both} & both
    for nh in pair_order(both, masks):
        g = game_picture(gd[grows[nh][0]:grows[nh][0] + grows[nh][1]])
        m = mod_picture(mb[mrows[nh][0]:mrows[nh][0] + mrows[nh][1]])
        if g is None or m is None:
            notes.append(f'{car} {nh:08x}: {"game" if g is None else "mod"} picture unreadable, left out'); continue
        rgb, grey = g
        if not rgb.any(): continue                               # nothing to paint: the game's stays
        blob, ch = avif(m, keep_area(rgb), grey or nh in masks, quality)
        ents.append((nh, blob, ch))
    if len(set(grows) - set(mrows)): notes.append(f'{car}: {len(set(grows) - set(mrows))} of the game\'s not in the mod')
    # the doorlines (CARS/<car>/TEXTURES.BIN, 512x512 A8R8G8B8): the mod's from its endscript's folder
    tp = find(game, f'CARS/{car}/TEXTURES.BIN')
    own = {}
    if tp:
        with open(tp, 'rb') as f: td = f.read()
        want = {bstring_hash(car + x): x for x in DOORLINES}
        own = {nh: (w, h, lv0) for nh, w, h, fmt, lv0 in textures(td) if nh in want and fmt == ARGB and lv0}
    for nh, x in ((bstring_hash(car + x), x) for x in DOORLINES):
        if nh not in own: continue
        w, h, lv0 = own[nh]
        m = dds_argb(mod.read(f'Installation/ModData/CARTEMPLATETEXTURES_/{car}/{car}{x}.dds'))
        if m is None or (w, h) != (512, 512):
            notes.append(f'{car}{x}: no 1024 picture in the mod'); continue
        import numpy as np
        rgb = np.frombuffer(lv0, np.uint8).reshape(512, 512, 4)[..., [2, 1, 0]]
        if not rgb.any(): continue
        blob, ch = avif(m, keep_area(rgb), x.endswith('_MASK'), quality)
        ents.append((nh, blob, ch))
    ents = [e for k in pair_order({e[0] for e in ents}, {hash_append(e[0], '_MASK') for e in ents} & {e[0] for e in ents})
            for e in ents if e[0] == k]
    path = os.path.join(out_dir, 'HQVINYLS', 'CARS', f'{car}.hqv')
    size = write(path, ents)
    return car, len(ents), size, notes


def hash_append(h, s):
    """bStringHash(name + s) from bStringHash(name)"""
    for c in s.encode('latin1'): h = (h * 33 + c) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return h


def pair_order(hashes, masks):
    """the pictures in the order they are stored: each vinyl followed by its _MASK (the runtime reads them together,
    and the page fetches the game folder in 1 MiB blocks: one block, not two)"""
    out = []
    for nh in sorted(hashes - masks):
        out.append(nh)
        m = hash_append(nh, '_MASK')
        if m in masks: out.append(m)
    seen = set(out)
    return out + sorted(h for h in hashes if h not in seen)


def write(path, ents):
    """ents in their stored order; the rows sorted by hash"""
    start = (16 + ROW * len(ents) + 15) & ~15
    head = bytearray(struct.pack('<4sIII', MAGIC, VERSION, len(ents), start))
    data, at, rows = bytearray(), start, []
    for nh, blob, ch in ents:
        rows.append((nh, at, len(blob), ch))
        data += blob; at += len(blob)
    for nh, off, size, ch in sorted(rows):
        head += struct.pack('<IIIHBB', nh, off, size, SIDE, ch, 0)
    head += bytes(start - len(head))
    whole = bytes(head) + bytes(data)
    import packcheck
    bad = packcheck.check(None, {f'HQVINYLS/CARS/{os.path.basename(path)}': whole})
    if bad: sys.exit(f'{path}: not written, tools/packcheck.py says: ' + '; '.join(why for _, why in bad[:20]))
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
    with open(path + '.part', 'wb') as f: f.write(whole)
    os.replace(path + '.part', path)
    return len(whole)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(usage=__doc__.split('\n\n')[1].strip())
    ap.add_argument('game')
    ap.add_argument('--mod', required=True, help="the mod's zip (High Quality Vinyls & Doorlines v1.0.zip) or folder")
    ap.add_argument('--quality', type=int, default=50, help='AVIF quality (default 50)')
    ap.add_argument('--jobs', type=int, default=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 2) - 1))
    ap.add_argument('--cars', help='only these cars (comma-separated)')
    ap.add_argument('--out', help='write HQVINYLS/ here (default: the game folder)')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if not find(a.game, 'SPEED2.EXE'): sys.exit(f'{a.game}: no SPEED2.EXE, not the game folder')
    from PIL import features
    if not features.check('avif'): sys.exit('Pillow without AVIF: pip install "Pillow>=11.3"')
    cars = Mod(a.mod).cars()
    if a.cars: cars = [c for c in cars if c in {x.strip().upper() for x in a.cars.split(',')}]
    if not cars: sys.exit(f'{a.mod}: no CARS/<car>/VINYLS.BIN, not the mod')
    jobs = [(a.game, a.mod, c, a.quality, a.out or a.game) for c in cars]
    total = 0
    with Pool(min(a.jobs, len(jobs))) as pool:
        for car, n, size, notes in pool.imap_unordered(one_car, jobs):
            total += size
            for x in notes: print('  ' + x)
            print(f'{car}: {n} pictures, {size / 1e6:.1f} MB', flush=True)
    print(f'HQVINYLS: {len(cars)} cars, {total / 1e6:.0f} MB')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

{"id": "AT001456", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/tools/inline_pick.py", "originalBytes": 4260, "originalSha256": "3a6b3f6e1b6d617a8362193e96453087c6030ec0787c442089a5f40106d8afdc", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 4260, "utf8TotalBytes": 4260}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pick the functions to inline (genall.py INLINE_LIST) from a call-count profile.

A race frame makes ~94,000 guest function calls; each costs a wasm call
(prologue, stack check, return) and the register stores and reloads around it
(LREGS).  Inlining removes that, but every call site gets its own copy, so the
pick is the most calls per byte of copies: a function qualifies when it is
called often (>= --min calls in the profile window), is at most --max x86
instructions, has direct call sites (indirect calls cannot be inlined) and
nothing genall.py refuses (tail jumps, run-time helpers, recursion,
overrides); then the best calls / (call sites x body size) go in until the
copies reach --budget bytes of C.  Measured in a race (web/tools/bench.mjs's
lockstep recipe): 1 MB (110 functions, 37 % of the calls) and 3 MB do the
same, 6 MB costs 3 % more cycles than 3 MB (more code to run through).

The profile: a COVERAGE=1 lift (COVERAGE=1 web/gen.sh), run through
tests/web/scripts/perf_cov.txt (covreset at the start of its window) with
COVREPORT=/save/cov.txt COVTOP=2000 in the environment, e.g.
  web/tools/bench.mjs --fps 120 --runs 1 --script /tests/web/scripts/perf_cov.txt
    --env COVREPORT=/save/cov.txt --env COVTOP=2000 (+ the recipe's lockstep env)
The exit report lists the most called functions ("<count>  sub_<addr>"
lines); this reads them from the run's log.

    tools/inline_pick.py <log> <gen/all> [--min N] [--max N] [--budget BYTES] > tools/inline_hot.txt
"""
import re, sys, os, glob, argparse, collections

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('log'); ap.add_argument('gen')
ap.add_argument('--min', type=int, default=30000, help='calls in the profile window (default 30000)')
ap.add_argument('--max', type=int, default=400, help='x86 instructions (default 400)')
ap.add_argument('--budget', type=int, default=1 << 20, help='bytes of C for the copies (default 1 MB)')
o = ap.parse_args()

log = open(o.log, errors='replace').read()
counts = {int(m.group(2), 16): int(m.group(1)) for m in re.finditer(r'^(?:\[\d+!\])?\s+(\d+)\s+sub_([0-9a-f]{8})\s*$', log, re.M)}
total = re.search(r'coverage: (\d+) calls in all', log)
if not counts: sys.exit('no "<count>  sub_<addr>" lines in the log (COVREPORT + COVTOP)')

hdr = re.compile(r'^/\* ===== sub_([0-9a-f]{8})  \((\d+) insns, (\d+) blocks\) ===== \*/')
fdef = re.compile(r'^void sub_([0-9a-f]{8})(_orig)?\(CPU')
deny = ('DISPATCH_TAIL', 'unsupported_insn', 'cpuid_shim', 'guest_hook', 'rdtsc_shim')
info, sites = {}, collections.Counter()
for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(o.gen, 'shard_*.c'))):
    text = open(f).read()
    for m in re.finditer(r'\bsub_([0-9a-f]{8})\(c\);', text): sites[int(m.group(1), 16)] += 1
    cur = None
    for part in re.split(r'(?m)^(?=/\* ===== sub_)', text):
        m = hdr.match(part)
        if not m: continue
        a = int(m.group(1), 16); d = fdef.search(part.split('\n', 2)[1] if '\n' in part else '')
        body = part.split('{', 1)[1] if '{' in part else ''
        info[a] = dict(n=int(m.group(2)), size=len(part), orig=bool(d and d.group(2)),
                       ok=not any(x in body for x in deny) and f'sub_{a:08x}(c)' not in body)

cand = []
for a, n in counts.items():
    i = info.get(a)
    if not i or not i['ok'] or i['orig'] or n < o.min or i['n'] > o.max or not sites[a]: continue
    cand.append((n / (sites[a] * i['size']), a, n, sites[a], i['n'], sites[a] * i['size']))
cand.sort(reverse=True)
pick, used, calls = [], 0, 0
for _, a, n, s, ins, g in cand:
    if used + g > o.budget: continue
    pick.append((a, n, s, ins)); used += g; calls += n
pick.sort()
tot = int(total.group(1)) if total else sum(counts.values())
print(f"# genall.py INLINE_LIST (web/gen.sh): {len(pick)} functions inlined at their direct call sites,")
print(f"# picked by tools/inline_pick.py from a race's call counts: {calls} of {tot} calls ({100 * calls / tot:.1f} %)")
print(f"# in the profile window, {used / 1048576:.1f} MB of C in copies.  address  calls  call sites  x86 instructions")
for a, n, s, ins in pick: print(f"{a:08x}  # {n} {s} {ins}")
print(f"inline_pick: {len(pick)} functions, {calls} of {tot} calls ({100 * calls / tot:.1f} %), {used / 1048576:.1f} MB of copies", file=sys.stderr)

END TEXT OBJECT AT001456

# ---------------- every conditional setcc ----------------
def cc(name, opc, a, b, want):
    T(f"set{name} ({a} ? {b})", [0xB8]+imm32(a)+[0x3D]+imm32(b)+[0x0F,opc,0xC2],
      {'edx':0}, expect={'edx':want})
cc('o' ,0x90, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1)
cc('b' ,0x92, 1, 2, 1);         cc('ae',0x93, 2, 1, 1)
cc('e' ,0x94, 5, 5, 1);         cc('ne',0x95, 5, 6, 1)
cc('be',0x96, 2, 2, 1);         cc('a' ,0x97, 3, 2, 1)
cc('s' ,0x98, 1, 2, 1);         cc('ns',0x99, 2, 1, 1)
cc('l' ,0x9C, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, 1);cc('ge',0x9D, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1)
cc('le',0x9E, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1, 1);cc('g' ,0x9F, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1)
cc('l_signed',0x9C, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0)
cc('b_unsigned',0x92, 1, 0xFFFFFFFF, 1)

# ---------------- x87 rounding control (RC field) ----------------
# fistp must follow the RC field of the control word.  The CRT's __ftol routine
# sets RC=11 (truncate); using nearbyint gives one too many for fractions >= 0.5.
FD = 0x00C40000
def _rc(name, cw, val, want):
    # fldcw [FD]; fld dword [FD+8]; fistp dword [FD+12]
    T(name, [0xD9,0x2D]+a32(FD) + [0xD9,0x05]+a32(FD+8) + [0xDB,0x1D]+a32(FD+12),
      {}, mem={FD:cw}, memf={FD+8:val}, expect={}, fmem={FD+12:want & 0xFFFFFFFF})

_rc("fistp RC=nearest 3.7 -> 4",   0x037F,  3.7,  4)
_rc("fistp RC=nearest 2.5 -> 2",   0x037F,  2.5,  2)   # round to even
_rc("fistp RC=nearest 3.5 -> 4",   0x037F,  3.5,  4)
_rc("fistp RC=trunc  3.7 -> 3",    0x0F7F,  3.7,  3)
_rc("fistp RC=trunc  -3.7 -> -3",  0x0F7F, -3.7, -3)
_rc("fistp RC=trunc  6.999 -> 6",  0x0F7F,  6.999, 6)
_rc("fistp RC=down   3.7 -> 3",    0x077F,  3.7,  3)
_rc("fistp RC=down   -3.2 -> -4",  0x077F, -3.2, -4)
_rc("fistp RC=up     3.2 -> 4",    0x0B7F,  3.2,  4)
_rc("fistp RC=up     -3.7 -> -3",  0x0B7F, -3.7, -3)

# x87 NaN propagation (Intel SDM vol. 1 table 4-7): with two NaN operands the
# result is the one with the larger significand, whichever is the
# destination.  The drift oracle found the integrator 0x5AA480 summing NaN
# garbage of unused state slots.
FN_ = 0x00C70000
T("fadd QNaN+QNaN -> larger significand (dst smaller)",
  [0xD9,0x05]+a32(FN_)+[0xD8,0x05]+a32(FN_+4)+[0xD9,0x1D]+a32(FN_+8),
  {}, mem={FN_:0x7FC00001, FN_+4:0x7FC00100}, expect={}, fmem={FN_+8:0x7FC00100})
T("fadd QNaN+QNaN -> larger significand (dst larger)",
  [0xD9,0x05]+a32(FN_+0x10)+[0xD8,0x05]+a32(FN_+0x14)+[0xD9,0x1D]+a32(FN_+0x18),
  {}, mem={FN_+0x10:0x7FC00100, FN_+0x14:0xFFC00001}, expect={}, fmem={FN_+0x18:0x7FC00100})
# x87 precision control (X87PC=1): fldcw [FP]; fld1; fdiv dword [FP+4] (3.0);
# fstp qword [FP+8].  PC=24 rounds the quotient to a float, PC=53 does not.
FP_ = 0x00C71000
def _pc(name, cw, lo, hi, base):
    T(name, [0xD9,0x2D]+a32(base) + [0xD9,0xE8] + [0xD8,0x35]+a32(base+4) + [0xDD,0x1D]+a32(base+8),
      {}, mem={base:cw}, memf={base+4:3.0}, expect={}, fmem={base+8:lo, base+12:hi})
_pc("fdiv 1/3 at PC=24 (CW 0x007F) -> float-rounded", 0x007F, 0x60000000, 0x3FD55555, FP_)
_pc("fdiv 1/3 at PC=53 (CW 0x027F) -> double",        0x027F, 0x55555555, 0x3FD55555, FP_+0x20)
_pc("fdiv 1/3 at PC=64 (CW 0x037F) -> double",        0x037F, 0x55555555, 0x3FD55555, FP_+0x40)
T("fmul QNaN*1.0 -> the NaN",
  [0xD9,0x05]+a32(FN_+0x20)+[0xD8,0x0D]+a32(FN_+0x24)+[0xD9,0x1D]+a32(FN_+0x28),
  {}, mem={FN_+0x20:0x3F800000, FN_+0x24:0x7FC0ABC0}, expect={}, fmem={FN_+0x28:0x7FC0ABC0})
# CRT __ftol pattern: fnstcw / or ah,0xc / fldcw / fistp
T("__ftol pattern (2.6+0.001 -> 2)",
  [0xD9,0x3D]+a32(FD+0x20) +                    # fnstcw [FD+0x20]
  [0x66,0xA1]+a32(FD+0x20) +                    # mov ax, [FD+0x20]
  [0x80,0xCC,0x0C] +                            # or ah, 0x0C
  [0x66,0xA3]+a32(FD+0x24) +                    # mov [FD+0x24], ax
  [0xD9,0x2D]+a32(FD+0x24) +                    # fldcw [FD+0x24]
  [0xD9,0x05]+a32(FD+0x28) +                    # fld dword [FD+0x28]
  [0xDB,0x1D]+a32(FD+0x2C),                     # fistp dword [FD+0x2C]
  {}, memf={FD+0x28:2.601}, expect={}, fmem={FD+0x2C:2})

# SSE2: the xmm forms of the MMX instructions work on all 128 bits.  A pack fills
# the low qword from the destination's elements and the high qword from the
# source's; an unpack interleaves the low (high) qwords of both into the whole
# register; the saturating adds and subtracts and the shifts do both halves, by
# one count.  They were lifted per 64-bit half (the VP6 decoder's SSE2 code).
# xmm0 = [x], xmm1 = [x+0x10] (or the operand itself), result [x+0x20].
X2 = [0x00C80000]
def _x2(name, op, a, b, want, m128=False):
    x = X2[0]; X2[0] += 0x40
    T(name + " (128-bit)", [0xF3,0x0F,0x6F,0x05]+a32(x)+[0xF3,0x0F,0x6F,0x0D]+a32(x+0x10)
      + op + (a32(x+0x10) if m128 else []) + [0xF3,0x0F,0x7F,0x05]+a32(x+0x20),
      {}, mem={x+4*k: v for k, v in enumerate(a + b)}, fmem={x+0x20+4*k: v for k, v in enumerate(want)})
_W1 = [0x7F010080, 0xFF7FFF80, 0x80001234, 0x00010000]; _W2 = [0x00FE0101, 0xFFFF0003, 0x7FFF0040, 0x80010100]
_B1 = [0x13121110, 0x17161514, 0x1B1A1918, 0x1F1E1D1C]; _B2 = [0xA3A2A1A0, 0xA7A6A5A4, 0xABAAA9A8, 0xAFAEADAC]
_S1 = [0x7FF08010, 0x00FF7FFF, 0xFF00C000, 0x40018000]; _S2 = [0x00207FF0, 0x0001FFFF, 0x0100C000, 0x3FFF0001]
_x2("packsswb xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x63,0xC1], _W1, _W2, [0x80807F7F, 0x0100807F, 0xFF037F7F, 0x807F7F40])
_x2("packssdw xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x6B,0xC1], [0x00007FFF, 0xFFFF8000, 0x00012345, 0xFFFE0000],
    [0x00000005, 0x80000000, 0xFFFFFFF0, 0x7FFFFFFF], [0x80007FFF, 0x80007FFF, 0x80000005, 0x7FFFFFF0])
_x2("packuswb xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x67,0xC1], _W1, _W2, [0x0000FF80, 0x010000FF, 0x0003FEFF, 0x00FFFF40])
_x2("packuswb xmm0,[m128]", [0x66,0x0F,0x67,0x05], _W2, _W1, [0x0003FEFF, 0x00FFFF40, 0x0000FF80, 0x010000FF], m128=True)
_x2("punpcklbw xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x60,0xC1], _B1, _B2, [0xA111A010, 0xA313A212, 0xA515A414, 0xA717A616])
_x2("punpckhbw xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x68,0xC1], _B1, _B2, [0xA919A818, 0xAB1BAA1A, 0xAD1DAC1C, 0xAF1FAE1E])
_x2("punpcklwd xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x61,0xC1], _B1, _B2, [0xA1A01110, 0xA3A21312, 0xA5A41514, 0xA7A61716])
_x2("punpckhwd xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x69,0xC1], _B1, _B2, [0xA9A81918, 0xABAA1B1A, 0xADAC1D1C, 0xAFAE1F1E])
_x2("punpckldq xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x62,0xC1], _B1, _B2, [0x13121110, 0xA3A2A1A0, 0x17161514, 0xA7A6A5A4])
_x2("punpckhdq xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0x6A,0xC1], _B1, _B2, [0x1B1A1918, 0xABAAA9A8, 0x1F1E1D1C, 0xAFAEADAC])
_x2("punpckhbw xmm0,[m128]", [0x66,0x0F,0x68,0x05], _B1, _B2, [0xA919A818, 0xAB1BAA1A, 0xAD1DAC1C, 0xAF1FAE1E], m128=True)
_x2("paddsw xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0xED,0xC1], _S1, _S2, [0x7FFF0000, 0x01007FFE, 0x00008000, 0x7FFF8001])
_x2("paddusb xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0xDC,0xC1], _S1, _S2, [0x7FFFFFFF, 0x00FFFFFF, 0xFF00FF00, 0x7FFF8001])
_x2("psubsb xmm0,xmm1", [0x66,0x0F,0xE8,0xC1], _S1, _S2, [0x7FD08020, 0x00FE7F00, 0xFE000000, 0x010280FF])
_x2("psubusw xmm0,[m128]", [0x66,0x0F,0xD9,0x05], _S1, _S2, [0x7FD00020, 0x00FE0000, 0xFE000000, 0x00027FFF], m128=True)
_x2("psllw xmm0,3", [0x66,0x0F,0x71,0xF0,0x03], _S1, _S2, [0xFF800080, 0x07F8FFF8, 0xF8000000, 0x00080000])
_x2("psrad xmm0,9", [0x66,0x0F,0x72,0xE0,0x09], _S1, _S2, [0x003FF840, 0x00007FBF, 0xFFFF8060, 0x002000C0])
_x2("psrlq xmm0,4", [0x66,0x0F,0x73,0xD0,0x04], _S1, _S2, [0xF7FF0801, 0x000FF7FF, 0x0FF00C00, 0x04001800])
_x2("psllq xmm0,xmm1 (count 12)", [0x66,0x0F,0xF3,0xC1], _S1, [12, 0, 0x55, 0x66], [0x08010000, 0xF7FFF7FF, 0x0C000000, 0x18000FF0])
# the count is the destination's own low qword: read before either half is shifted
_x2("psrlw xmm0,xmm0 (count 4)", [0x66,0x0F,0xD1,0xC0], [4, 0, 0xF00FABCD, 0x8000FFF0], [0, 0, 0, 0],
    [0x00000000, 0x00000000, 0x0F000ABC, 0x08000FFF])
# all 64 bits of the count: 2^32+4 is more than 15 (each word becomes its sign), not 4
_x2("psraw xmm0,xmm1 (count 2^32+4)", [0x66,0x0F,0xE1,0xC1], _S1, [4, 1, 0x55, 0x66], [0x0000FFFF, 0x00000000, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x0000FFFF])
# A callee that returns past its caller (tools/retpast.txt), in the shape of the
# CRT's x87 2^x core (0x7653de): a range check (fcompp, fnstsw into the frame at
# ebp, test 0x41, jne) and, out of range, 'pop eax' -- its own return address --
# and a ret that goes to its caller's caller.  The test calls F (+0x12), F calls
# H (+0x21) and adds 1 and sets ebx only when H comes back to it.  ZF, CF and
# SF start at 1; out of range H's test leaves them 0, which the early return
# hands on (CF and SF check the FLAGABI lift: H's own jne reads only ZF).  With
# RETEIP=0 (a ret only pops) H still writes c->eip: F compares it.
RP = 0x00C90000
def _rp(name, x, rp, res, expect, env=None):
    T(name, [0xD9,0x05]+a32(rp) + [0xE8,0x07,0,0,0] + [0xD9,0x1D]+a32(rp+8) + [0xC3]   # fld [rp]; call F; fstp [rp+8]
      + [0xE8,0x0A,0,0,0, 0xD9,0xE8, 0xDE,0xC1, 0xBB,1,0,0,0, 0xC3]                     # F: call H; fld1; faddp; mov ebx,1
      + [0xD9,0xC0, 0xD9,0xE1, 0xD9,0x05]+a32(rp+4) + [0xDE,0xD9]                       # H: fld st0; fabs; fld [limit]; fcompp
      + [0x9B, 0xDD,0xBD,0x60,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF, 0xF6,0x85,0x61,0xFF,0xFF,0xFF,0x41]       # fnstsw [ebp-0xa0]; test [ebp-0x9f],0x41
      + [0x75,0x01, 0xC3, 0x58, 0xDD,0xD8, 0xD9,0x05]+a32(rp+12) + [0xC3],              # jne; ret | pop eax; fstp st0; fld [rp+12]
      {'ebp':rp+0x200, 'ebx':0, 'zf':1, 'cf':1, 'sf':1}, memf={rp:x, rp+4:100.0, rp+12:7.0}, expect=expect, fmemf={rp+8:res},
      calls=(0x12, 0x21), retpast=(0x21,), env=env)
_rp("call returning past its caller: in range", 3.0, RP, 4.0, {'ebx':1})
_rp("call returning past its caller: out of range", 1000.0, RP+0x400, 7.0, {'ebx':0, 'zf':0, 'cf':0, 'sf':0, 'eax':0x00401017})
_rp("call returning past its caller: in range, RETEIP=0", 3.0, RP+0x800, 4.0, {'ebx':1}, env={'RETEIP':'0'})
_rp("call returning past its caller: out of range, RETEIP=0", 1000.0, RP+0xC00, 7.0, {'ebx':0, 'zf':0, 'cf':0, 'sf':0, 'eax':0x00401017},
    env={'RETEIP':'0'})
T("pushal/popal", [0x60, 0xB8,0x99,0,0,0, 0x61],   # pushad; mov eax,0x99; popad
  {'eax':0x11223344,'ecx':0x55667788}, expect={'eax':0x11223344,'ecx':0x55667788})
FC = 0x00C60000
T("fstp tbyte / fld tbyte (3.75)",

T("addsd xmm0,[m]", [0xF2,0x0F,0x10,0x05]+a32(FC+0x60)+[0xF2,0x0F,0x58,0x05]+a32(FC+0x68)+[0xF2,0x0F,0x11,0x05]+a32(FC+0x70),
  {}, mem={FC+0x60:0x00000000, FC+0x64:0x3FF00000, FC+0x68:0x00000000, FC+0x6C:0x40000000},
  fmem={FC+0x70:0x00000000, FC+0x74:0x40080000})
T("movhlps", [0x0F,0x28,0x05]+a32(FC+0x80)+[0x0F,0x12,0xC0]+[0x0F,0x29,0x05]+a32(FC+0x90),
  {}, mem={FC+0x80:1,FC+0x84:2,FC+0x88:3,FC+0x8C:4},

# v12na: MMX<->SSE conversions (0x73392f cvtpi2ps trapped in the race)

# ---------------- switch jump tables (JTSWITCH=1 only) ----------------
# Lifted as a C switch whose cases check the table entry in guest memory (the
# tables are written there with mem=); without JTSWITCH the jmp is a tail call
# through the dispatcher, which this harness does not have.
if os.environ.get('JTSWITCH', '') == '1':
    _B = 0x00401000
    # cmp eax,2; ja default; jmp [eax*4+tab]; case0/1/2: mov ebx,10/20/30; default: mov ebx,99; ret; tab
    _JT1 = ([0x3D]+imm32(2)+[0x77,0x1C, 0xFF,0x24,0x85]+imm32(_B+0x29)
            + [0xBB]+imm32(10)+[0xEB,0x13] + [0xBB]+imm32(20)+[0xEB,0x0C] + [0xBB]+imm32(30)+[0xEB,0x05]
            + [0xBB]+imm32(99) + [0xC3] + imm32(_B+0x0E)+imm32(_B+0x15)+imm32(_B+0x1C))
    _JT1M = {_B+0x29:_B+0x0E, _B+0x2D:_B+0x15, _B+0x31:_B+0x1C}
    for _v, _w in ((0, 10), (1, 20), (2, 30), (3, 99), (0xFFFFFFFF, 99)):
        T(f"switch [eax*4] (eax={_v:#x})", _JT1, {'eax':_v, 'ebx':0}, mem=_JT1M, expect={'ebx':_w})
    # MSVC's two-level switch: cmp eax,3; ja default; movzx ecx, byte [eax+idx]; jmp [ecx*4+tab];
    # case0/1: mov ebx,10/20; default: mov ebx,99; ret; idx = 1,0,1,0; tab
    _JT2 = ([0x3D]+imm32(3)+[0x77,0x1C, 0x0F,0xB6,0x88]+imm32(_B+0x29) + [0xFF,0x24,0x8D]+imm32(_B+0x2D)
            + [0xBB]+imm32(10)+[0xEB,0x0C] + [0xBB]+imm32(20)+[0xEB,0x05] + [0xBB]+imm32(99) + [0xC3]
            + [1,0,1,0] + imm32(_B+0x15)+imm32(_B+0x1C))
    _JT2M = {_B+0x29:0x00010001, _B+0x2D:_B+0x15, _B+0x31:_B+0x1C}
    for _v, _w, _x in ((0, 20, 1), (1, 10, 0), (2, 20, 1), (3, 10, 0), (4, 99, None)):
        _e = {'ebx':_w}
        if _x is not None: _e['ecx'] = _x
        T(f"two-level switch (eax={_v})", _JT2, {'eax':_v, 'ebx':0, 'ecx':0x55}, mem=_JT2M, expect=_e)
    # instructions that leave the flags and the index alone between them (sub_00468160's shape):
    # cmp eax,1; push esi; ja default; mov ecx,esi; jmp [eax*4+tab]; case0/1: mov ebx,10/20;
    # default: mov ebx,99; pop esi; ret; tab
    _JT3 = ([0x3D]+imm32(1)+[0x56, 0x77,0x17, 0x8B,0xCE, 0xFF,0x24,0x85]+imm32(_B+0x26)
            + [0xBB]+imm32(10)+[0xEB,0x0C] + [0xBB]+imm32(20)+[0xEB,0x05] + [0xBB]+imm32(99) + [0x5E, 0xC3]
            + imm32(_B+0x11)+imm32(_B+0x18))
    _JT3M = {_B+0x26:_B+0x11, _B+0x2A:_B+0x18}
    for _v, _w, _c in ((0, 10, 0x1234), (1, 20, 0x1234), (2, 99, 0x77)):   # default: ja before the mov
        T(f"switch after push/mov (eax={_v})", _JT3, {'eax':_v, 'ebx':0, 'ecx':0x77, 'esi':0x1234}, mem=_JT3M, expect={'ebx':_w, 'ecx':_c, 'esi':0x1234})

# cmpxchg whose flags are dead (the next cmp overwrites them), with ZF=0 before it: the store must still
# happen (the lifted test read c->zf, which a dead-flags lift never computed)
T("cmp edx,1; cmpxchg [m],ecx; cmp eax,ebx", [0x83,0xFA,0x01, 0x0F,0xB1,0x0D]+a32(0x00C00100)+[0x39,0xD8],
  {'eax':5,'ecx':9,'ebx':5,'edx':0}, mem={0x00C00100:5}, expect={'eax':5,'zf':1}, fmem={0x00C00100:9})
# a straight run longer than the lifter's block limit (discover()'s maxins, 4000): the rest must still run
T("4100 x inc eax", [0x40]*4100, {'eax':0}, expect={'eax':4100})

# =====================  GENERATOR / RUNNER  =====================
BASE = 0x00401000
def build():
    fns=[]; body=[]
    for i,t in enumerate(TESTS):
        L = RawLifter(t['code'] + b'\xc3', base=BASE, comments=False)
        L.retpast = {BASE + x for x in t['retpast']}
        keep = {k: os.environ.get(k) for k in t['env']}; os.environ.update(t['env'])
        try:
            code,_ = L.lift(BASE)
            more = [L.lift(BASE + x)[0] for x in t['calls']]
        except Unsupported as e:
            print(f"  !! {t['name']}: could not be lifted ({e})"); fns.append(None); continue
        finally:
            for k, v in keep.items():
                if v is None: os.environ.pop(k, None)
                else: os.environ[k] = v
        names = {f"sub_{BASE:08x}": f"test_{i}", **{f"sub_{BASE + x:08x}": f"test_{i}_{x:x}" for x in t['calls']}}
        for a, b in names.items():
            code = code.replace(a, b); more = [s.replace(a, b) for s in more]
        body += [f"void test_{i}_{x:x}(CPU *c);" for x in t['calls']] + more + [code]
        fns.append(f"test_{i}")
    return fns, body

REGS = ['eax','ecx','edx','ebx','esp','ebp','esi','edi']
FLAGS = ['cf','pf','af','zf','sf','of','df']

def gen_c(fns, body):
    o=[]
    o.append('#include "cpu.h"\n#include <stdio.h>\n#include <string.h>\n#include <math.h>')
    o.append('void mem_commit(uint32_t,uint32_t);')
    o.append('guest_fn_t g_dtab[DISPATCH_TEXT_SIZE];   /* empty: indirect calls go to the stub below */')
    o.append('void dispatch_indirect(CPU*c,uint32_t a){(void)c;(void)a;}')
    o.append('void unsupported_insn(CPU*c,uint32_t a,const char*m){(void)c;(void)a;(void)m;fprintf(stderr,"TRAP 0x%x %s\\n",a,m);}')
    o.append('void guest_hook(CPU*c,uint32_t a){(void)c;(void)a;}')
    o.append('void cpuid_shim(CPU*c){(void)c;} uint64_t rdtsc_shim(void){return 0;}')
    # LREGS=1 (tools/lregs.py): the lifted bodies name the registers in locals; the harness below does not
    lr = os.environ.get('LREGS', '') == '1'
    if lr: o.append('#undef RG_\n#define RG_(x) _r_##x')
    o.append('\n'.join(body))
    if lr: o.append('#undef RG_\n#define RG_(x) c->x')
    o.append('static CPU cpu; static CPU *const c=&cpu;')
    o.append('#define STK 0x00B00000u')
    o.append('static int pass=0, fail=0;')
    o.append('static void chk(const char*t,const char*f,uint32_t got,uint32_t want){')
    o.append('  if(got==want){pass++;} else {fail++;')
    o.append('    printf("  \\033[31mFAIL\\033[0m %-38s %s = 0x%08x (expected 0x%08x)\\n",t,f,got,want);}}')
    o.append('static void chkf(const char*t,const char*f,float got,float want){')
    o.append('  if(memcmp(&got,&want,4)==0){pass++;} else {fail++;')
    o.append('    printf("  \\033[31mFAIL\\033[0m %-38s %s = %.9g (expected %.9g)\\n",t,f,(double)got,(double)want);}}')
    o.append('int main(void){ mem_init(); mem_commit(0x00000000u,0x01000000u); mem_fault_handler_install();')
    for i,t in enumerate(TESTS):
        if fns[i] is None: continue
        nm = t['name'].replace('"','\\"')
        o.append(f'  /* --- {i}: {nm} --- */')
        o.append('  { memset(&cpu,0,sizeof cpu); cpu.esp=STK; cpu.top=0; cpu.fcw=0x037f;')
        for r,v in t['setup'].items():
            o.append(f'    cpu.{r} = 0x{v & 0xffffffff:x}u;')
        for a,v in t['mem'].items():
            o.append(f'    MR32(0x{a:x}u) = 0x{v & 0xffffffff:x}u;')
        for a,v in t.get('memf',{}).items():
            o.append(f'    MRF32(0x{a:x}u) = {v!r}f;')
        o.append('    uint32_t esp0 = cpu.esp;')
        o.append('    PUSH32(0xDEADC0DEu);')
        o.append(f'    {fns[i]}(&cpu);')
        o.append(f'    chk("{nm}","esp balance",cpu.esp,esp0);')
        for k,v in t['expect'].items():
            if k=='ah_and':
                mask,want = v
                o.append(f'    chk("{nm}","ah&0x{mask:02x}",((cpu.eax>>8)&0x{mask:02x}u),0x{want:02x}u);')
            elif k in REGS:
                o.append(f'    chk("{nm}","{k}",cpu.{k},0x{v & 0xffffffff:x}u);')
            elif k in FLAGS:
                o.append(f'    chk("{nm}","{k}",cpu.{k},{v}u);')
        for a,v in t['fmem'].items():
            o.append(f'    chk("{nm}","mem[0x{a:x}]",MR32(0x{a:x}u),0x{v & 0xffffffff:x}u);')
        for a,v in t.get('fmemf',{}).items():
            o.append(f'    chkf("{nm}","fmem[0x{a:x}]",MRF32(0x{a:x}u),{v!r}f);')
        o.append('  }')
    o.append('  printf("\\n  ISA tests: \\033[32m%d passed\\033[0m, %s%d failed\\033[0m\\n",')
    o.append('         pass, fail?"\\033[31m":"", fail);')
    o.append('  return fail?1:0; }')
    return '\n'.join(o)

if __name__=='__main__':
    fns, body = build()
    src = gen_c(fns, body)
    os.makedirs('gen', exist_ok=True)
    open('gen/isatest.c','w').write(src)
    print(f"gen/isatest.c written ({len(TESTS)} tests)")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""lan_trace.py -- compare how LAN race instances see each other's cars.

  tools/lan_trace.py <run dir>            (reads <run dir>/i*/cars.csv)
  tools/lan_trace.py a.csv b.csv [...]

Each instance writes NFSU2_CAR_TRACE (runtime/autotest.c): per frame the
wall-clock time (CLOCK_REALTIME, the same clock for every instance on this
Mac; in the browser a worker's time origin plus its monotonic clock, so
instances started on either side of a correction of the system clock -- WSL
makes them -- are that far apart: a WorldTimer offset of a second or more
in the last lines, and ~50 m errors for every pair with that instance, while
the game's own [racenet] "their race clock ... off ours" says tens of ms;
lan-pair.mjs's clock.csv next to each trace now lines them up), the frame cap, WorldTimer and every race car with a flag for the local
player's car.  Frames whose top package is not the race HUD (pre-race
screen, results) are left out when the trace says so.  For every pair (owner A, viewer B) this tool finds A's car in
B's car list (the index whose positions stay closest to A's own trace) and
reports, over the time both are racing and A's car moves (> 2 m/s):

  err     distance between where B shows A's car and where A had it at the
          same instant (median / 95th percentile / max, metres)
  lag     err / speed: the display delay that would explain it (ms)
  jumps   frames in which B's view of A's car moved more than
          max(2 m, 3 x speed x frame time) -- a teleport / rubber band;
          compare with the jumps in A's own trace (the game resetting a
          crashed car onto the track is a real teleport, seen by everyone).
          The frame time is the longer of the wall-clock step and the game
          time the frame simulated (B's WorldTimer: the next row's minus
          this row's, as a row's cars are logged after the frame's
          simulation and its WorldTimer before it).  After a stall of an
          instance (for example 106 and 208 ms) a network race's
          world clock catches up in one frame and every car moves that far,
          which is no jump.  A jump within BACK_S seconds after a frame in
          which B's WorldTimer went back by more than 50 ms (the client's world
          clock set back to the host's after stalls of both instances:
          -217.8 ms, then the shown car 5.5 m back) is
          listed apart ("after a clock correction") and not counted; so is a
          step of the game's far-car mode (B shows A's car with a speed under
          0.5 m/s while A moves: from about 145 m between the cars the game
          updates a remote car in steps every 0.1 s; seen at 143-149 m), and a jump within STALL_S
          seconds after a frame of A or B that took longer than STALL_MS (a
          stalled instance: its car stops for the others, or it stops showing
          them, and the game corrects afterwards; on a loaded Mac, load 40-70,
          115-270 ms, then a 2.3 m snap).  Both are
          printed, so a run on a busy machine still shows them
  fps     frames per second of each instance while racing, and its cap

and the same split by the distance between B's own car and A's car: within
NEAR metres (racing together) and farther.  The game treats a car far from
the player differently: from about 150-200 m its shown speed is 0 and it
moves in steps of several metres every 0.1 s (netfix/session6 race 1, at
180-207 m), and beyond 300 m it is 1-2.5 m off (netfix/lanrace-final; E2's
150-300 m corrections) -- seen in the traces, not traced in the code.
tests/net/lan_race.sh judges the near part.

It also prints each instance's own racing time span and frame rate, and how
far each instance's WorldTimer is from the first instance's (the race host
in the LAN scripts: clients synchronise their world clock to it).
"""
import csv, glob, math, os, sys
from bisect import bisect_left

NEAR = 150.0                                  # metres between the viewer's car and the shown car
BACK = -0.050                                 # s: a frame whose world step is below this set the clock back
BACK_S = 1.0                                  # s after it: a jump there is the correction showing
FAR_V = 0.5                                   # m/s: a shown speed below this while the owner moves = the far-car mode
STALL_MS = 100.0                              # a frame longer than this: the instance stalled
STALL_S = 1.0                                 # s after the stall's end: a jump there is its correction

def stall_ends(times):
    """wall times at which a frame of an instance ended after more than STALL_MS"""
    return [times[i] for i in range(1, len(times)) if (times[i] - times[i - 1]) * 1000.0 > STALL_MS]

def after(ends, t):
    i = bisect_left(ends, t + 1e-9)
    return i > 0 and t - ends[i - 1] <= STALL_S

def results_frame(path):
    """first frame of the results screen in the instance's log, if any"""
    log = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(path), 'log.txt')
    try:
        with open(log, errors='replace') as f:
            for line in f:
                if 'screen UI_PostRaceResults.fng' in line and line.startswith('[fng] f='):
                    return int(line.split('f=')[1].split()[0])
    except OSError:
        pass
    return None

def load(path):
    rows = []
    stop = results_frame(path)
    with open(path) as f:
        for r in csv.DictReader(f):
            try:
                t = float(r['t']); n = int(r['n'])
            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                continue
            if stop is not None and int(r['frame']) >= stop:
                break                         # the race is over (results screen)
            cars = []
            for i in range(n):
                try:
                    cars.append((r[f'c{i}local'] == '1', float(r[f'c{i}x']), float(r[f'c{i}y']),
                                 float(r[f'c{i}z']), float(r[f'c{i}v'])))
                except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                    cars.append(None)
            if r.get('hud') == '0':
                continue                      # results / post-race scene, not racing
            rows.append((t, float(r['cap'] or 0), int(r['worldtimer'] or 0), cars))
    return rows

WT_HZ = 4000.0                                # WorldTimer ticks per second

def world_steps(rows):
    """per row: the game time (s) its frame simulated"""
    return [(rows[i + 1][2] - rows[i][2]) / WT_HZ if i + 1 < len(rows) else 0.0 for i in range(len(rows))]

def own_track(rows):
    tr = []
    ws = world_steps(rows)
    for i, (t, cap, wt, cars) in enumerate(rows):
        for c in cars:
            if c and c[0]:
                tr.append((t, c[1], c[2], c[3], c[4], ws[i])); break
    return tr

def interp(tr, ts, t):
    i = bisect_left(ts, t)
    if i <= 0 or i >= len(tr): return None
    a, b = tr[i - 1], tr[i]
    if b[0] - a[0] > 0.5: return None
    k = (t - a[0]) / (b[0] - a[0]) if b[0] > a[0] else 0
    return tuple(a[j] + k * (b[j] - a[j]) for j in (1, 2, 3, 4))

def pct(v, p):
    if not v: return float('nan')
    v = sorted(v); return v[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * (len(v) - 1) + 0.5))]

def main(argv):
    if len(argv) == 1 and os.path.isdir(argv[0]):
        files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(argv[0], 'i*', 'cars.csv')))
    else:
        files = argv
    if len(files) < 2:
        print('need two or more traces'); return 2
    data = {os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(f)) or f: load(f) for f in files}
    # The instances' wall clocks can differ (a page's clock is its worker's time origin + now(), the origin the wall
    # clock as the worker started: pages started across a WSL clock step read that far apart, ~0.5 s in 2 of 3 runs
    # on 2026-11-03).  lan-pair.mjs's clock.csv next to each trace has the trace clock of every "[ctclock]" line
    # against when lan-pair saw it by its own monotonic clock; the least difference is the instance's offset.
    offs = {}
    for f in files:
        k = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(f)) or f
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(f), 'clock.csv')) as cf:
                o = [float(r['arrived_ms']) / 1000.0 - float(r['trace_s']) for r in csv.DictReader(cf)]
            if o: offs[k] = min(o)
        except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError):
            pass
    if len(offs) == len(data):
        ref = offs[next(iter(data))]
        for k in data:
            d = offs[k] - ref
            if abs(d) > 0.002: print(f'{k}: its trace clock read {-d * 1000:+.1f} ms off the first one\'s (clock.csv): corrected')
            data[k] = [(t + d, cap, wt, cars) for t, cap, wt, cars in data[k]]
    elif offs:
        print('clock.csv missing for some instance: traces lined up by their own wall clocks')
    tracks = {k: own_track(v) for k, v in data.items()}
    print('instance  rows  racing span (s)  fps   cap (fps)  own car samples')
    for k, rows in data.items():
        if not rows: print(f'{k:8s}  no rows'); continue
        span = rows[-1][0] - rows[0][0]
        caps = sorted(set(round(1 / r[1]) if r[1] > 0 else 0 for r in rows))
        print(f'{k:8s}  {len(rows):5d}  {span:8.1f}  {len(rows) / span if span > 0 else 0:6.1f}  {caps}  {len(tracks[k])}')
    worst = 0.0
    def own_jumps(tra):
        n = 0
        for p, q in zip(tra, tra[1:]):
            dt = max(q[0] - p[0], q[5]); mv = math.dist(p[1:4], q[1:4])
            if dt > 0 and q[4] > 2.0 and mv > max(2.0, 3 * q[4] * dt): n += 1
        return n
    for a, tra in tracks.items():
        if len(tra) < 10: continue
        print(f'{a} own car: {own_jumps(tra)} jumps in its owner\'s own trace (resets onto the track)')
        ts = [p[0] for p in tra]
        for b, rows in data.items():
            if b == a or not rows: continue
            ncar = max(len(r[3]) for r in rows)
            best = None
            for j in range(ncar):
                d = []
                for t, cap, wt, cars in rows[::10]:
                    if j >= len(cars) or not cars[j] or cars[j][0]: continue
                    p = interp(tra, ts, t)
                    if p: d.append(math.dist(p[:3], cars[j][1:4]))
                if len(d) > 5:
                    m = sorted(d)[len(d) // 2]
                    if best is None or m < best[0]: best = (m, j)
            if not best:
                print(f'{a} -> {b}: car not found'); continue
            j = best[1]
            err, lag, jumps, n = [], [], 0, 0
            part = {True: [[], 0, 0, 0, 0], False: [[], 0, 0, 0, 0]}   # near / far: errors, jumps, after a correction, far-car steps, after a stall
            stalls = sorted(stall_ends(ts) + stall_ends([r[0] for r in rows]))
            prev = None
            ws = world_steps(rows)
            back_t = None
            for i, (t, cap, wt, cars) in enumerate(rows):
                if ws[i] < BACK: back_t = t
                if j >= len(cars) or not cars[j]: prev = None; continue
                c = cars[j]
                me = next((x for x in cars if x and x[0]), None)
                near = me is not None and math.dist(me[1:4], c[1:4]) <= NEAR
                p = interp(tra, ts, t)
                if p and p[3] > 2.0:
                    e = math.dist(p[:3], c[1:4]); err.append(e); lag.append(e / p[3] * 1000); n += 1
                    part[near][0].append(e)
                if prev and p and p[3] > 2.0:
                    dt = max(t - prev[0], ws[i]); mv = math.dist(prev[1], c[1:4])
                    if dt > 0 and mv > max(2.0, 3 * p[3] * dt):
                        if back_t is not None and t - back_t <= BACK_S: part[near][2] += 1
                        elif len(c) > 4 and abs(c[4]) < FAR_V: part[near][3] += 1
                        elif after(stalls, t): part[near][4] += 1
                        else: jumps += 1; part[near][1] += 1
                prev = (t, c[1:4])
            worst = max(worst, pct(err, 0.95) if err else 0)
            print(f'{a} car as seen by {b} (index {j}): {n} samples, err median {pct(err, .5):.2f} m, '
                  f'p95 {pct(err, .95):.2f} m, max {max(err) if err else float("nan"):.2f} m; '
                  f'lag median {pct(lag, .5):.0f} ms, p95 {pct(lag, .95):.0f} ms; jumps {jumps}')
            for k, label in ((True, f'within {NEAR:.0f} m of the viewer'), (False, 'farther')):
                e, jn, jb, jf, js = part[k]
                print(f'    {label}: {len(e)} samples, err median {pct(e, .5):.2f} m, p95 {pct(e, .95):.2f} m; '
                      f'jumps {jn}' + (f' (+{jb} after a clock correction, not counted)' if jb else '')
                      + (f' (+{jf} far-car steps, shown speed 0, not counted)' if jf else '')
                      + (f' (+{js} after a stall over {STALL_MS:.0f} ms, not counted)' if js else ''))
    for k, rows in data.items():
        g = [(rows[i][0] - rows[i - 1][0]) * 1000.0 for i in range(1, len(rows))]
        g = [x for x in g if x > STALL_MS]
        if g: print(f'{k} frames longer than {STALL_MS:.0f} ms while racing: {len(g)}, longest {max(g):.0f} ms')
        b = [x for x in world_steps(rows) if x < BACK]
        if b: print(f'{k} WorldTimer set back by more than {-BACK * 1000:.0f} ms in {len(b)} frame(s), '
                    f'largest {min(b) * 1000:.1f} ms')
    # world clocks: every instance against the first one (the race host in
    # the LAN scripts; clients slave their WorldTimer to it, 0x5891B0)
    keys = list(data)
    if keys and data[keys[0]]:
        h = [(r[0], r[2]) for r in data[keys[0]]]
        ht = [x[0] for x in h]
        for k in keys[1:]:
            d = []
            for t, cap, wt, cars in data[k]:
                i = bisect_left(ht, t)
                if 0 < i < len(h) and h[i][0] - h[i - 1][0] < 0.5:
                    a, b = h[i - 1], h[i]
                    d.append((wt - (a[1] + (b[1] - a[1]) * (t - a[0]) / (b[0] - a[0]))) / 4000.0)
            if d:
                print(f'{k} WorldTimer - {keys[0]} WorldTimer at the same instant: median {pct(d, .5) * 1000:+.1f} ms, '
                      f'p5 {pct(d, .05) * 1000:+.1f} ms, p95 {pct(d, .95) * 1000:+.1f} ms')
    return 0

if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The language packs: LANGPACKS/<language> in the game folder, from the
"Multi 13 languages" mod for NFSU2 (KyoriAsh, nfsmods.xyz/mod/5749), from
TraduMix's and MixMods' Brazilian Portuguese translation, from PLProjekt's
Polish one, from VileStuff's English subtitles, from muntazam's Turkish
translation (its fonts, with tools/lang/turkish.json's text), from GameHunter's
Hungarian one, from Clark X.'s Ukrainian one, from ROXOR's and PINĎA & syn's Czech one
(with tools/lang/czech.json's texts), from MixerX's Slovak one and from the Greek pack
tools/greekfont/build_greek.py makes (tools/lang/greek.json's texts).

    tools/langpacks.py <game folder> [--multi13 <mod folder>] [--ptbr <translation folder>]
                       [--pl <installer>] [--subs <subtitles folder>] [--tr <translation folder>]
                       [--hu <installer>] [--uk <translation folder>] [--cz <installer>]
                       [--sk <translation folder>] [--el <Greek pack folder>]

Each source builds its own languages' packs; the others are left as they are.

<mod folder> holds every archive of the mod extracted into it, Core and the
dubs (nfsug2Multi13Core.rar, nfsug2Multi13{Fr,De,It,Es,Ja,Ru}Dub.rar; the
English dub is the game's own).  The dubs need RAR 7's unrar (`unrar x`):
libarchive (bsdtar, Windows' tar) cannot read their dictionary size.

The mod's own installer copies its files over the game's and sets the
registry; the port reads them from a folder per language instead
(runtime/language.c, fileio.c's language pack), so every player picks one
for themselves and the game folder stays as it was.  A pack holds only what
differs from the game folder: a file there is read in place of the game's file
of the same path.

  - the dubbed speech banks, from each dub's sdat*.viv: speech/UG2_Speech_FR,
    _GR, _IT, _SP and _JP are the game's own names for French, German, Italian,
    Spanish and Japanese; Russian's stands in for the English bank.  The rest of
    the archive is the game's (the cutscene sound, nisaudio) or its music,
    which stays the game's.
  - the dubbed movies (Lang/Movies/<Xx>), and the Danish, Dutch and Swedish EA
    logos
  - the full Chinese, Japanese and Thai texts (the game folder's are short
    early versions) with the fonts drawn for them (LanguageTexturesGl), and
    Japanese's in-game textures (GlobalB_ja); Thai's with its ordinal suffixes
    emptied (TEXTS)
  - Russian, which takes English's place: its text, fonts and credits

<translation folder> is the Brazilian Portuguese translation's text archive
extracted (v1.1.1, 2026, "Tradução Need for Speed Underground 2.rar" from
mixmods.com.br's "[NFSU2] Tradução/Dublagem Português PT-BR" page; the older
V1.1 from joao13traducoes.com, password "João13", differs in one text), or any
folder below which it has LANGUAGES/English.bin.  Portuguese takes English's
place as Russian does: its text (accented in the game's own fonts) and
credits, and the game folder's own Brazilian Portuguese memory-card texts
("Carregado." for "Load complete.").  The page's AI dub is not used, nor
joao13's Extra Options mod (for its ShowSubs: the port shows the subtitles
itself, runtime/language.c).

<installer> is either installer of the Polish translation (v1.1, 2009,
NFSU2PLv1.1US.exe or NFSU2PLv1.1UK.exe, from its archive at portal24h.pl), or
the folder they are in.  It is read, never run: an Astrum InstallWizard
package, whose files are gzip streams.  Polish takes English's place as Russian
does: its text spells the Polish letters with accented ones the game's fonts
have (ę is ¿, ł is î, ś is â ...), and its fonts' textures
(LanguageTextures.bin, and one in GLOBALA.BUN) draw those as the Polish ones;
also its memory-card texts and credits.  Two texts it left in English, the
race HUD's DRAFT and the tip about it, get Polish ones (PL_TEXTS).  The rest of the
installer is a Polish SPEED2.EXE, the game folder's own GLOBALB.BUN, the
British game's Corsa and 106 (this game folder has them) and a script that
hides the movies.

<subtitles folder> is VileStuff's "English Subtitles Fixed" mod (v1.0,
nfsmods.xyz/mod/5286) extracted.  Its Binary endscript (script/main.end)
gives 105 of English's texts: the movies' lines (the PSA, the tutorials, the
story) whole and with who speaks them, where the game folder's stop at their
first apostrophe ("But if you").  English's pack holds the game's English.bin
with those texts, and with it the port shows the movies' subtitles in English
too (runtime/language.c).  The mod is installed with Binary and needs the
Extra Options mod's ShowSubs; neither is used.

<translation folder> (--tr) is muntazam's Turkish translation (v1.1, 2024,
"Need for Speed Underground 2 Turkish Translation Patch" at moddb.com)
extracted: its archive holds an Inno Setup installer, nfsu2tr11.exe, which
`innoextract nfsu2tr11.exe` unpacks (into app/) without running it; or any
folder below which it has LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures.bin.  Turkish takes
English's place as Polish does, with its own text: tools/lang/turkish.json,
every one of the game's texts translated from English (by the label the
game's code and menus look it up by, its hash where none is known) and the
memory-card texts.  The translation gives its fonts: their textures
(LanguageTextures.bin, and one in GLOBALA.BUN) draw accented letters the
game's fonts have as the Turkish ones (ş is ÿ, ı is í, ğ is ý, İ is Í, Ş is
þ, Ğ is Ý), and the text is written in those.  The credits stay the game's.  The port
shows the movies' subtitles itself (runtime/language.c), so the Extra Options
mod the translation asks for is not needed.

<installer> (--hu) is GameHunter's Hungarian translation (v1.1, 2005, by
L_zooltan; nfs_underground2.exe from gamehunter.hu or magyaritasok.hu), or the
folder it is in.  It is read, never run: an Astrum InstallWizard package, as
the Polish one.  Hungarian takes English's place as Portuguese does: its text,
which spells ő and ű as õ and û (the game's fonts have no ő or ű, and
Hungarian texts of the time wrote them so), its memory-card texts and credits.

<translation folder> (--uk) is Clark X.'s Ukrainian translation ("Need for
Speed Underground 2 - Ukrainian.exe", 2022, from kuli.com.ua) unpacked with
`innoextract` (into app/), never run; or any folder below which it has
LANGUAGES/English.bin and GLOBAL/GLOBALA.BUN.  Ukrainian takes English's place
as Russian does, on the Russian pack's fonts (its LanguageTextures.bin and
GLOBALA.BUN are those): its text writes І і Ї ї Є є as bytes 0xE2-0xE7 of
their glyph table, the rest in Russian's order; also its memory-card texts and
credits.  The rest of the installer is not used: a GlobalB.lzc that differs
from the game's in one byte (the ™ of a shave gel's name) and two files the
game never reads (LANGUAGES/Labels.bin, Largest.bin).
<installer> (--cz) is ROXOR's and PINĎA & syn's Czech translation (v1.1, 2004;
nfsu2cz-v1.1.exe in nfs-underground-2-cz.zip from abcgames.cz's "Need for Speed:
Underground 2" translations page), the zip or the folder it is in.  It is read, never
run: a Clickteam Patch Maker patch, which carries the files whole in Clickteam's own
deflate (clickteam_files).  Czech takes English's place as Hungarian does: its text and
memory-card texts.  The text writes the letters with the caron and u with the ring
without them (c, r, s, z, e, u for č, ř, š, ž, ě, ů), as the translation says itself
("partial diacritics"): the game's fonts have only the acute ones.  The translation was
made on German's text, so it left some of it in German (the gamepad help lines,
colours, countries, Xbox Live, PlayStation 2 and demo messages) and the movies' lines
empty, as German's dubbed text has them; tools/lang/czech.json has those texts in
Czech, in the translation's spelling, by their hash (CZ_TEXT).  The patch's German.bin
and LOCALE_GERMAN.loc (the same translation for the German game) are not used.

<translation folder> (--sk) is MixerX's Slovak translation (v1.0, 2011; NFSU2UK_SK.exe
in nfs-underground-2-uk-sk.zip from the same page, or NFSU2US_SK.exe for the American
game, whose language files are the same) unpacked with `7z x` (an NSIS installer,
never run); or any folder below which it has Languages/Swedish.bin and
Global/GLOBALA.BUN.  It replaces the Swedish files in the Windows game; here Slovak
takes English's place as Polish does: its text, written in Windows-1250 with every
Slovak letter, the fonts' textures it comes with (LanguageTextures.bin, GLOBALA.BUN),
which draw those letters, its memory-card texts and credits, all as they are.  Not
used: its own SPEED2.EXE and CD image (the movies' subtitles are shown by
runtime/language.c), and the American one's Corsa and 106.
<Greek pack folder> (--el) is the LANGPACKS/greek that tools/greekfont/build_greek.py
makes from the game's own files: its English.bin with tools/lang/greek.json's texts and
the fonts' glyph records for the Greek letters, LanguageTextures.bin and GLOBALA.BUN with
those letters drawn into the fonts' textures, and the memory-card texts.  Greek takes
English's place as Polish does.
Rerunning it copies only what changed, each as a new file (a copy of the game
folder made of hard links keeps its own).  Prints what each pack holds.  Each
file the game reads as a chunk file (.bin, .bun, .lzc) is checked as the game
reads it (tools/packcheck.py: its chunks, texture packs and texts) before it is
written; one that fails stops it, not written.
"""

def find(root, rel):
    """rel under root, each part matched case-insensitively; None if missing"""
    cur = root
    for part in rel.split('/'):
        if not os.path.isdir(cur): return None
        hit = next((n for n in os.listdir(cur) if n.lower() == part.lower()), None)
        if hit is None: return None
        cur = os.path.join(cur, hit)
    return cur


def game_name(game, rel):
    """rel spelled as the game folder spells it, as far as it has it"""
    out, cur = [], game
    for part in rel.split('/'):
        hit = next((n for n in os.listdir(cur) if n.lower() == part.lower()), None) if os.path.isdir(cur) else None
        out.append(hit or part); cur = os.path.join(cur, hit or part)
    return '/'.join(out)


def viv_entries(path):
    """(name, offset, size) of a BIG4/BIGF archive (EA's .viv)"""
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        head = f.read(16)
        if head[:3] != b'BIG': sys.exit(f'{path}: not a .viv archive')
        n, hdr = struct.unpack('>II', head[8:16]); d = f.read(hdr - 16)
    out, q = [], 0
    for _ in range(n):
        off, size = struct.unpack('>II', d[q:q + 8]); q += 8
        e = d.index(b'\0', q); out.append((d[q:e].decode('latin1'), off, size)); q = e + 1
    return out


class Pack:
    def __init__(self, game, lang):
        self.game, self.root, self.files, self.bytes = game, os.path.join(game, 'LANGPACKS', lang), 0, 0
        self.made = set()

    def target(self, rel):
        return os.path.join(self.root, game_name(self.game, rel))

    def check(self, rel, data=None, src=None):
        """stops before a file the game would read wrong is written (tools/packcheck.py)"""
        if not rel.lower().endswith(packcheck.CHUNKED): return
        key = f'LANGPACKS/{os.path.basename(self.root)}/{game_name(self.game, rel)}'
        bad = packcheck.check(self.game, {key: data if data is not None else src})
        if bad: sys.exit(f'{key}: not written, tools/packcheck.py says: ' + '; '.join(why for _, why in bad))

    def same_as_game(self, rel, data=None, src=None):
        g = find(self.game, rel)
        if not g or os.path.getsize(g) != (len(data) if data is not None else os.path.getsize(src)): return False
        if src: return filecmp.cmp(src, g, shallow=False)
        with open(g, 'rb') as f: return f.read() == data

    def add_file(self, src, rel):
        if self.same_as_game(rel, src=src): return
        dst = self.target(rel)
        self.check(rel, src=src)
        if not (os.path.exists(dst) and filecmp.cmp(src, dst, shallow=False)):
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst), exist_ok=True); shutil.copyfile(src, dst + '.new'); os.replace(dst + '.new', dst)
        self.files += 1; self.bytes += os.path.getsize(dst); self.made.add(dst)

    def add_data(self, data, rel):
        if self.same_as_game(rel, data=data): return
        dst = self.target(rel)
        self.check(rel, data=data)
        if not (os.path.exists(dst) and os.path.getsize(dst) == len(data) and open(dst, 'rb').read() == data):
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst), exist_ok=True)
            with open(dst + '.new', 'wb') as f: f.write(data)
            os.replace(dst + '.new', dst)
        self.files += 1; self.bytes += len(data); self.made.add(dst)

    def drop_stale(self):
        """what an earlier run put here and this one did not"""
        for d, dirs, names in os.walk(self.root, topdown=False):
            for n in names:
                if os.path.join(d, n) not in self.made: os.remove(os.path.join(d, n))
            if not os.listdir(d): os.rmdir(d)


def done(p, lang):
    p.drop_stale()
    print(f'{lang:10} {p.files:3} files {p.bytes / 1048576:8.1f} MB  {p.root if p.files else "(none needed)"}')


def multi13(mod, game):
    missing = [s for _, s, _ in FILES if not find(mod, s)]
    missing += [f'Lang/Sdata/sdat{x.lower()}.viv' for x in DUBS.values() if not find(mod, f'Lang/Sdata/sdat{x.lower()}.viv')]
    missing += [f'Lang/Movies/{x}' for x in DUBS.values() if not find(mod, f'Lang/Movies/{x}')]
    if missing: sys.exit(f'{mod}: the mod is not all there (extract every archive into it), missing:\n  ' + '\n  '.join(missing))

    for lang in LANGS:
        p = Pack(game, lang)
        for l, src, rel in FILES:
            if l != lang: continue
            if (lang, rel) in TEXTS:
                with open(find(mod, src), 'rb') as f: p.add_data(with_texts(f.read(), TEXTS[lang, rel])[0], rel)
            else: p.add_file(find(mod, src), rel)
        if lang in DUBS:
            viv = find(mod, f'Lang/Sdata/sdat{DUBS[lang].lower()}.viv')
            with open(viv, 'rb') as f:
                for name, off, size in viv_entries(viv):
                    if not name.lower().startswith('speech/ug2_speech'): continue
                    f.seek(off); p.add_data(f.read(size), name)
            mdir = find(mod, f'Lang/Movies/{DUBS[lang]}')
            for n in sorted(os.listdir(mdir)): p.add_file(os.path.join(mdir, n), f'MOVIES/{n}')
        done(p, lang)


def ptbr(src, game):
    root = next((d for d, _, _ in os.walk(src) if find(d, 'LANGUAGES/English.bin')), None)
    if not root: sys.exit(f'{src}: no LANGUAGES/English.bin below it, not the translation')
    missing = [s for s, _ in PTBR if not find(root, s)]
    if missing: sys.exit(f'{root}: the translation is not all there, missing:\n  ' + '\n  '.join(missing))
    p = Pack(game, 'portuguese')
    if p.same_as_game('LANGUAGES/English.bin', src=find(root, 'LANGUAGES/English.bin')):
        sys.exit(f'{root}: its LANGUAGES/English.bin is the game\'s own, not the translation')
    for s, rel in PTBR: p.add_file(find(root, s), rel)
    loc = find(game, 'memcard/LOCALE_BRAZILIAN_PORTUGUESE.loc')
    if loc: p.add_file(loc, 'memcard/LOCALE_ENGLISH.loc')
    done(p, 'portuguese')


def astrum_files(path):
    """{path in the game folder, lower-cased: data} of an Astrum InstallWizard 2
    installer.  It ends with the package's header offset, a block of n bytes, n
    (0xffffffff for none, in the older Hungarian one) and the magic; the
    header (big-endian words) gives where the files start, and they end where
    it begins.  Each file: a 0x40-byte record whose word 0x2c is its name's
    length, the name ("<InstallDir>\\...", each byte's bit i stored as bit i^6),
    the offset its data ends at, the data: a gzip stream, or the file as it is
    (a few bytes)."""
    with open(path, 'rb') as f: d = f.read()
    if d[-8:] != struct.pack('<II', 0x0b1c2d3e, 0x12345678): sys.exit(f'{path}: not an Astrum InstallWizard installer')
    n = struct.unpack('<I', d[-12:-8])[0]
    if n == 0xffffffff: n = 0
    head = struct.unpack('<I', d[-16 - n:-12 - n])[0]
    hdr = struct.unpack('>59I', d[head:head + 236])
    pos = hdr[48]
    if pos + hdr[49] != head: sys.exit(f'{path}: an Astrum package of another layout')
    out = {}
    while pos < head:
        size = struct.unpack('<I', d[pos + 0x2c:pos + 0x30])[0]
        name = bytes(sum((b >> i & 1) << (i ^ 6) for i in range(8)) for b in d[pos + 0x40:pos + 0x40 + size])
        end = struct.unpack('<I', d[pos + 0x40 + size:pos + 0x44 + size])[0]
        rel = name.decode('latin1').split('\\', 1)[1].replace('\\', '/')
        data = d[pos + 0x44 + size:end]
        out[rel.lower()] = gzip.decompress(data) if data[:3] == b'\x1f\x8b\x08' else data
        pos = end
    return out


def pl(src, game):
    exe = src if os.path.isfile(src) else next(
        (os.path.join(src, n) for n in sorted(os.listdir(src), reverse=True) if n.lower().startswith('nfsu2pl') and n.lower().endswith('.exe')), None)
    if not exe: sys.exit(f'{src}: no NFSU2PLv1.1US.exe or NFSU2PLv1.1UK.exe, not the translation')
    files = astrum_files(exe)
    missing = [s for s, _ in PL if s.lower() not in files]
    if missing: sys.exit(f'{exe}: not the translation, missing:\n  ' + '\n  '.join(missing))
    p = Pack(game, 'polish')
    text = {h: bytes(PL_LETTERS.get(c) or ord(c) for c in t) for h, t in PL_TEXTS.items()}
    files['languages/polish.bin'] = with_texts(files['languages/polish.bin'], text)[0]
    for s, rel in PL: p.add_data(files[s.lower()], rel)
    done(p, 'polish')


def str_hash(s):
    """the game's hash of a text's label (bStringHash)"""
    h = 0xffffffff
    for c in s.encode('ascii'): h = (h * 33 + c) & 0xffffffff
    return h


def tr_bytes(s):
    """a Turkish text in the letters of the translation's fonts"""
    bad = sorted(set(c for c in s if c not in TR_LETTERS and c not in TR_LATIN))
    if bad: sys.exit(f'{TR_TEXT}: {bad} in "{s}", letters the fonts lack')
    return bytes(TR_LETTERS.get(c) or ord(c) for c in s)


def tr(src, game):
    root = next((d for d, _, _ in os.walk(src) if find(d, 'LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures.bin')), None)
    if not root: sys.exit(f'{src}: no LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures.bin below it, not the translation (innoextract its nfsu2tr11.exe)')
    missing = [s for s, _ in TR if not find(root, s)]
    if missing: sys.exit(f'{root}: the translation is not all there, missing:\n  ' + '\n  '.join(missing))
    p = Pack(game, 'turkish')
    if p.same_as_game('LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures.bin', src=find(root, 'LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures.bin')):
        sys.exit(f'{root}: its LANGUAGES/LanguageTextures.bin is the game\'s own, not the translation')
    with open(TR_TEXT, encoding='utf-8') as f: t = json.load(f)
    texts = {int(k, 16) if k.startswith('0x') else str_hash(k): tr_bytes(v) for k, v in t['texts'].items()}
    for rel in ('LANGUAGES/English.bin', 'memcard/LOCALE_ENGLISH.loc'):
        if not find(game, rel): sys.exit(f'{game}: no {rel}')
    with open(find(game, 'LANGUAGES/English.bin'), 'rb') as f: data, changed = with_texts(f.read(), texts, whole=True)
    print(f'turkish: {changed} of its {len(texts)} texts differ from English\'s')
    p.add_data(data, 'LANGUAGES/English.bin')
    with open(find(game, 'memcard/LOCALE_ENGLISH.loc'), 'rb') as f:
        p.add_data(with_loc(f.read(), [tr_bytes(s) for s in t['memcard']]), 'memcard/LOCALE_ENGLISH.loc')
    for s, rel in TR: p.add_file(find(root, s), rel)
    done(p, 'turkish')


def hu(src, game):
    exe = src if os.path.isfile(src) else next(

    if not exe: sys.exit(f'{src}: no nfs_underground2.exe, not the translation')

    missing = [s for s, _ in HU if s.lower() not in files]
    if missing: sys.exit(f'{exe}: not the translation, missing:\n  ' + '\n  '.join(missing))
    p = Pack(game, 'hungarian')
    for s, rel in HU: p.add_data(files[s.lower()], rel)
    done(p, 'hungarian')
